subject: Re: Redwood demo + stakeholder mapping / procurement steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie O'Neill <jamie.oneill@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Great convo today — next steps & stakeholder map

Hi Jamie,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the context on your platform and the latency/cost sensitivity for your search summarization workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Stakeholders we heard: you (product/owner), Chris Rivera (platform lead), Lina Kaur (security), and Procurement.
- Decision criteria: latency < 150ms 95th on 1k qps, predictable per-token cost, and SOC2 + controls for data retention.
- Procurement path: Procurement will review SOW + SOC2 artifact; if any SLA exceptions needed we should surface them early.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a short stakeholder map and a draft SOW for Procurement/Security review (attached).
2) Neha from our CS team will join a 30-min call next week to walk technical ops and security through KV-caching and retention controls.
3) If Procurement requests any SLA adjustments we’ll start an internal approval for a buying-process exception (discounts or SLA wording).

Are the stakeholders above correct? If there’s an internal procurement contact email you want looped in, please share.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: 415-555-0192
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: SOW-draft-v1.pdf

From: Jamie O'Neill <jamie.oneill@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Great convo today — next steps & stakeholder map

Thanks Marissa — that all looks right. A couple clarifications from Procurement & Security side:

- Procurement will need a versioned SOW and a short SOC2 summary (what controls are in scope). Can you include retention defaults and whether logs/audit trails are available?
- Our security team will likely ask about data residency and whether you offer VPC/private deployments — they may ask for a brief runbook.
- We have an internal SLA requirement for 99.95% monthly availability for production endpoints; if Redwood’s standard terms are lower Procurement will request an SLA exception and we’ll need approval from Finance.

Procurement contact is procurement@enterprisecorp.com — looping them now. Please also include any standard enterprise discounts you offer for committed usage.

—Jamie
Director of Platform Engineering | EnterpriseCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood demo — EnterpriseCorp procurement asks / request for internal approval

Aditya / Neha — forwarding notes from today’s follow-up with EnterpriseCorp (see below). Quick TL;DR: Procurement will request a 99.95% monthly SLA and confirmation of SOC2 controls + retention defaults. They may also ask for a short discount tied to a 12-month committed usage.

Could you advise on the approval path for: 
- SLA exception to 99.95% (our standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% for hosted tiers unless Dedicated contract is purchased)
- A potential one-time onboarding credit or baseline discount for a 12-month commit (they suggested they’re evaluating competitors)

I’ve attached the draft SOW and SOC2 summary we plan to send to Procurement. If you need a cost impact estimate I can pull usage profiles from the call.

Thanks — prefer a quick sync if that’s easier.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.pdf, SOC2-summary.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood demo — EnterpriseCorp procurement asks / request for internal approval

Marissa — thanks for the context. My read:

- SLA: We can approve an exception to 99.95% for hosted API if they sign a 12-month committed capacity (Dedicated would be better long-term but Procurement is often sensitive to CapEx). I’ll need to record the exception with Legal and Finance; can you confirm expected committed spend (ARR equivalent) so I can route?
- Discount/credits: We can offer a one-time onboarding credit up to $50k or a 10% committed-use discount for 12 months, whichever is lower. Finance sign-off required if >$25k.

Neha — please prepare a short note for Security on retention defaults, KV caching, and audit logging that we can include in the SOC summary (or attach).

If you can confirm the numbers, I’ll kick off the internal approval (Legal + Finance) and draft the exception memo.

-Aditya
Senior Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie O'Neill <jamie.oneill@enterprisecorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Great convo today — next steps & stakeholder map

Jamie / Procurement team — following up with the artifacts and next steps. Attached: SOW-draft-v1.pdf and a short SOC2-summary.docx from Neha. Key points: 

- SLA: We’ve provisionally approved an exception to 99.95% monthly availability contingent on a 12-month committed usage contract (Aditya has started the approval flow; Finance requires committed-spend confirmation).
- Pricing: We can offer either a $50k onboarding credit or a 10% committed-use discount for a 12-month commit (Finance sign-off required if credit > $25k).
- Security: Retention defaults are 30 days for KV cache, 365 days for audit logs; VPC/private deployment is available for Private customers — we can include a runbook if you prefer.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm estimated committed spend range (ballpark is fine) so we can finalize approvals.
2) If Procurement wants the SLA exception language, we’ll prep a draft SOW addendum and route for signatures.
3) Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ENT-2026-042 — I’ll upload the signed addendum to DocuSign when ready.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call to close items.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.pdf, SOC2-summary.docx
